summary.one_liner: CodeFuse-ChatBot is an open-source, Chinese-documented AI assistant from Ant's CodeFuse team that uses multi-agent scheduling, retrieval-augmented generation, and sandboxes to support software development and DevOps tasks.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a multi-agent scheduling core that can be configured to build interactive agents, plus tool learning and a sandbox for running code. It supports repository-level code analysis and file-level code generation, and document analysis that combines a knowledge base with a knowledge graph. It can build DevOps-specific knowledge bases, crawl specified URLs for information, and process documents through loading, cleaning and chunking into vector and graph databases. It works with open-source LLMs and embedding models for offline private deployment, and also supports the OpenAI API. A web UI launched via examples/start.sh is mentioned for configuration.
use_cases: Ask questions about a local code repository
Generate code within an existing project
Build a private knowledge base for DevOps documentation
Query documents with retrieval and knowledge graphs
Crawl web pages for information to feed an LLM
how_to_run: Configure server_config.py, then open the web page and start the chat service
notable: Repository-wide code understanding and file-level code generation
Combines document knowledge base with knowledge graph
Sandbox environment for safe code execution
Supports both offline open-source LLMs and the OpenAI API
caveats: Tested only on Windows and X86 macOS per the README; requires user-installed NVIDIA drivers for GPU use
Apple Silicon users may need to install qpdf via brew first
Model support table is sparse: only chatgpt and a codellama-34b-int4 entry marked 'coming soon' for HuggingFace
